turns.user: What layer cycle-time window do I need for a 1 m high wall, 20 mm nozzle, static yield stress 2 kPa, Athix 0.8 Pa/s, open time 45 min, starting 10 min after mixing?
turns.text:
I’ll check the buildability calculator for the cycle-time window and identify any geometry assumptions needed.
The calculator requires a trial cycle time even to determine the allowable window. I’ll use a provisional cycle time; the calculated bounds will determine whether any schedule is feasible.
**There is no feasible layer cycle-time window under the calculator’s default wall geometry.**

| Constraint | Cycle time |
|---|---:|
| Minimum for plastic stability, including safety factor | **198.0 s/layer** |
| Maximum before open time expires | **21.0 s/layer** |

These bounds do not overlap. Even without the safety factor, the minimum is **123.7 s/layer**.

Assumptions: **10 mm layer height, 100 layers, 23.69 mm single-filament wall thickness, density 2,100 kg/m³, safety factor 1.5**, and elastic-modulus/yield-stress ratio **25**. Your yield stress is treated as the value **at extrusion**.

The physical verdict is **non-printable**: free-wall buckling is an additional limitation. At the provisional **20 s/layer** schedule, the plastic-stability calculation requires either initial yield stress of approximately **16.24 kPa** or Athix of **7.92 Pa/s**, holding the other property fixed. These changes alone do not resolve buckling.

Consider a thicker or braced wall and faster structural buildup through accelerator, VMA, or reduced w/b, then reassess extrusion and stability experimentally.
